prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 服务器安全基线核查记录 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 8 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "受检服务器唯一编号" · longest unbreakable word 20px · one-line width 138px
  col 2: header "系统账户口令强度" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 3: header "外部网络访问开放" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 4: header "日志留存天数达标" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 123px
  col 5: header "漏洞补丁更新状态" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 6: header "高危端口关闭数量" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 7: header "近三十天告警次数" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 8: header "应急联系人确认情况" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 138px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Every column is squeezed to roughly the same narrow width, so four headers (col 1, 4, 7, 8) fall to three lines and break words badly — 受检服务|器唯一编|号, 应急联|系人确|认情况. The table also stops ~30px short of the dashed box, so width that could have relieved the wrapping is simply left unused; the data cells themselves stay clean and readable."},"B":{"grade":"good","why":"Fills the full 720px and keeps the six middle headers on two clean lines (系统账户/口令强度, 漏洞补丁/更新状态), so scanning across a row is easy. Weak spot is the hierarchy: the row-identifier column is the narrowest, forcing 受检服务/器唯一编/号 into three lines and splitting 编号, and the last column splits 情况 — the two columns a reader anchors on are the ones that look cramped."},"C":{"grade":"poor","why":"Col 1 and col 8 are given generous width while the six middle columns are crushed to three lines each, and those wraps cut words in half: 系统账|户口令|强度, 外部网|络访问|开放, 漏洞补|丁更新|状态, 高危端|口关闭|数量. The header band becomes tall and hard to parse, and the cramped middle columns are exactly where the comparison data lives."},"D":{"grade":"poor","why":"Same crushed middle columns as C with the same broken words (账|户, 补|丁, 端|口), plus an extreme imbalance: the last header 应急联系人确认情况 sits on one very wide single line while the other seven columns wrap to two or three lines.
